headline: Wired: a probe heads back to planetary-defense test asteroids
pages: Wired reports that a space probe is returning to the pair of asteroids where NASA tested planetary defense technology. Four years ago, NASA tried to change the orbit of the asteroid Dimorphos, which circles the larger Didymos, by hitting it with a spacecraft. The idea is to nudge a dangerous object so it arrives at the meeting point with Earth a little later and simply misses. Wired notes that blowing a large rock into pieces, as in the movies, is not ideal. The story points to the asteroid Apophis, which astronomers predict will pass Earth in mid-April 2029 at about 19,000 miles, roughly 12 times closer than the moon, and be visible to the naked eye.
Detection has improved greatly, but the ability to deflect a threatening object in time remains the missing link. Source: Wired.
